warm.interpretation: Unpaused world progression changes the complete semantic core and world clock between actual saves. No byte differences are normalized. This case qualifies active voice identity/playback, not full host-state equality.

cold.interpretation: Unpaused world progression changes the complete semantic core and world clock between actual saves. No byte differences are normalized. This case qualifies active voice identity/playback, not full host-state equality.

visual_review.finding: Both composed post-audio frames show X alive at full HP, the Zero meter empty and native death rings in the intro. Captures are reviewed independently, not required to match during running simulation.
visual_review.limits: No original artwork, particle mechanic, HUD, campaign transition or audio-output/PCM qualification follows from the screenshots.

limits: Same physical Windows machine, exact compiled candidate, fixed X/P1 + Zero/P2 intro, offline only; no cross-build or heterogeneous claim.
Original host-published inputs reach authored record25 and cause eight ordinary strength4 contact losses; no HP, actor, audio or success-flag writes.
Only the exact new PST is copied to a fresh private cold profile; warm caches, settings and native memory cards are not transferred.
Private slot20 source group3/16 vocal is qualified. Slot23 shared death effect is observed active in the snapshots but its complete restored lifetime is not qualified here.
Voice activity, positive envelope, source bank/start/pitch/ADSR, all nine owner tags, static registers/modes/banks and saved decoder cursor are checked. The source bank bytes remain immutable.
All saved priority bytes are zero; native restoration of nonzero priorities remains unverified.
Simulation and DSP advance between saves; complete host core/world clock differences are retained explicitly. No unpaused full-state equality or once-world claim.
The complete event suffix across each load is retained; selected voice has END_STOP with no intervening KEYON/KEYOFF in that suffix. No old KEYON is paired with a post-load terminal.
No mapped user save/load hotkeys, rewind, rollback, network state transfer, native invalid-state rejection, PCM comparison, additional audio families or full F33 pass.
The earlier menu-paused failure is a setup failure. The exact native STOP caller after menu entry was not captured; no source-call qualification is inferred.
Native memory cards are preserved; old save-state compatibility/migration is not required.
